A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 4 June 1835 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1).

merge_ruling.for_merge: One surname, one forename initial, and nine days apart in the same newspaper: the Chicago Democrat prints `J. H. Barnard` on 4 June 1835 and `J. B. Barnard` on 13 June 1835. A compositor who set B for H once would produce exactly this pair.
merge_ruling.against_merge: The middle initials are B and H, both printed, and neither card carries a trade, an address, an arrival or any source that is not a notice — so there is no anchor to attach the other to and nothing reached decides which reading is the man's. R3: either two men or one man mis-set. Until T-1120 the pair was invisible, because M2 folded `J. H. Barnard` onto `J. B. Barnard` on the leading initial alone.

roles.note: PRINTED AGAINST THIS NAME IN THE 1833-1835 PRESS and carried here from the newspaper gazetteer (T-1254, by tools/derive_resident_roles.py). The gazetteer holds its trades on the PERSON record and not on a single issue, so the bound is the run of this person's own dated mentions, 1835-06-04 to 1835-06-04, and the grade is `inferred`: the paper printed the trade, and the resident programme's identity rule tied the printing to this card. The scene date falls outside that run, so this role does not stand in the 1835 view.
